key_insight: Bayesian inference applied to photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade—at the bulk or at specific transport-layer interfaces.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster diagnosis of failure mechanisms and more targeted passivation or stack-design strategies to improve perovskite device lifetime.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to observed optoelectronic behavior
Bayesian inference used to generate spatially resolved parameter maps during aging
evidence_signal: The authors tracked inferred parameter maps over time under 70 °C full-spectrum sunlight and found strong spatially non-uniform degradation, with the largest changes concentrated near perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: The inferred maps depend on model assumptions and image quality, so mis-specified transport/recombination physics could bias the identified degradation origin.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
